Research Domains: Behavioral Ecology and Evolutionary Biology of Poeciliid Fishes
Cognition, Behavioral Syndromes, and Social Behavior
Ecological and Experimental Evolution in Controlled Environments

Techniques Used: Cross-species comparative behavioral experiments in ecologically controlled mesocosms and lab tanks
Dichotomous/binomial mate-choice assays (conspecific vs heterospecific; large vs small female stimuli)
Cognitive-behavioral test batteries: sociability, detour-reaching, route learning, scototaxis
Video tracking and recording with EthovisionXT15 and cameras (IR, Nikon)
Multivariate statistics: Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), Discriminant Function Analysis (DFA), Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with lavaan
Model selection and comparison: GLMs, AIC-based selection, RMSEA, GFI, and other fit indices; Kruskal–Wallis, Dunn’s tests; t-tests and chi-square tests
Data handling: common garden and mesocosm experiments; side-bias handling in mate-choice tests
Data visualization and scripting in R; SPSS used in some papers; QGIS for mapping
Data & Platforms: Ecological and behavioral datasets across Poeciliid fishes (four species; Limia perugiae; Poecilia spp.)
Experimental settings: predator-free outdoor mesocosms (~800 gallons) and standard laboratory tanks (40-L, 5-L)
Behavioral tracking tools: EthovisionXT15; infrared video; Nikon D5200; other camera setups
Software: R (v4.x), SPSS (v25–29), lavaan for SEM, QGIS 3.2, possibly Noldus Ethovision
Data repositories and reproducibility: Dryad data (example DOI referenced: 10.5061/dryad.rfj6q57ht)
Application Areas: Behavioral Ecology and Evolutionary Biology of livebearing fishes
Sexual selection and mating-system evolution in Poeciliids
Cognition, learning, and behavioral syndromes in animals
Animal welfare and humane experimental design in aquatic research
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Cross-species and cross-context comparative analyses to identify conserved vs. divergent mating-system-related phenotypes
Investigation of sex-specific trait expression and dominance patterns in hybrids, revealing sex-linked regulatory effects
Integration of ecologically grounded experiments with advanced multivariate statistics (SEM, LDA, DFA) to uncover cognitive-behavioral syndromes
Linking behavioral ecology with evolutionary genetics and speciation processes in Poeciliids
Commitment to data transparency, reproducibility, and open data sharing
Summary Description: Dr. Ingo B. Schlupp is a leading figure in behavioral ecology and evolutionary biology focusing on Poeciliid fishes. His work spans mating systems, sexual selection, female cognition and behavioral syndromes, cross-species comparisons of mating tactics, geographic variation in mate choice, and the role of hybridization and postzygotic isolation in speciation. He also contributes to welfare-oriented aquaculture research by examining how environmental enrichment affects growth, health, reproduction, and welfare in livebearing fishes. Methodologically, he employs predator-free mesocosm and common-garden experiments, advanced multivariate statistics (SEM with lavaan, LDA, DFA), robust nonparametric and parametric tests, and state-of-the-art behavioral tracking, underscoring a strong commitment to experimental rigor, reproducibility, and cross-disciplinary collaboration.
